title: Yet another ‘free to download’ app that charges to be used at all

This reduces the appeal of the much-quoted “cancel anytime” statement because of course they don’t mind if you cancel. They’ve already got hundreds of your dollars. And for a system that makes such exorbitant promises (which I was very excited to put to the test) I find it very disconcerting that they do not have enough faith in their product to offer a lower tier or free trial - even for a couple days. Very disconcerting- these practices always seem scammy to me, so a fair warning to you all before you let an app psychoanalyse you for 20 minutes only to demand exorbitant funds before you see any results or have any actual idea of how this ‘magical revolutionary adhd cure’ app works. Also they spelt distractions wrong in their introduction. A pretty poor oversight for a service that values itself so highly, don’t you think?

author: Liwar1624

title: I don’t actually know what this app does
body:
This app did exactly what I saw a multilevel marketing company do.
This app did exactly what I saw a timeshare company do.

What is it? 
It relies on the sunk cost fallacy, making you fill out answers for all of 10 minutes, sign up, etc, but then before the app has done anything other than ask you a bunch of questions on what could literally be a quizlet form, BAM 💥 unskippable paywall.

Don’t worry though, because the paywall assures you that this uses research from all the big universities that do research.
And that people reviewed it really highly and that it helped them very much.

Give us money. Guarantee results AFTER 30 days.
30 day automatic billing.

Truth be told I don’t even actually know what this app does. Other than the Quizlet forms… I haven’t seen a single second of functionality from the app.
Is it games? Is it short videos? Is it an AI Chatbot? Is it a soothing meditation generator? I have no clue there’s a paywall.


And don’t get me wrong I am more than happy to pay for an app.
But before I’m willing to give out my money, I wanna have some semblance of an idea of what the app is actually offering.

I get that running an AI thing is expensive. The API cost alone.
But you know what isn’t expensive?
Developers screen recording a video of their app, actually working, and putting that in the tutorial process so you can see what their app is actually about.



So here it is. My two star review.
Two and not one because when you sort reviews, the most critical ones are always two stars with reason and not just a strong emotion.

Even if you just made the first day free. Even if you just filmed a video. Even if you just showed us the user interface and greyed everything out so that we can’t use it.

title: Stay Away – An Expensive Subscription For A Worse ChatGPT
body:
MindFlow AI markets itself as a specialized ADHD and task-management coach, but in reality it is just a simple chat interface running on what feels like an outdated OpenAI model. Many of the heavily advertised features simply do not exist.

The app is extremely minimal: You are always thrown back into the same chat interface, chats are not properly saved, there is no real history and therefore no meaningful long-term learning or personalized adaptation. To-do lists only exist as plain text inside the chat: Nothing you can check off, no structured overview, no boards. Reminders or notifications for tasks: Not available. For a product that claims to support people with ADHD, this completely misses the point. On top of that: The app often responds very slowly and has already frozen on me multiple times while handling tasks.

Particularly misleading is the so-called progress system: You appear to gain experience points and “level up”, but in practice it all feels extremely generic, follows a fixed template, and is barely personalized – more cosmetic than genuinely helpful. This might work as a very rough starting point if you have absolutely no idea how to structure yourself and you are fine working only inside a chat. For almost everyone else, it will be largely useless.

In the end, MindFlow AI is simply a worse, more limited version of ChatGPT behind a paywall. No real added value, but fewer options.

The lack of a proper free trial and the fact that you are pushed straight into a subscription makes it look like a very transparent cash grab: The less you can test beforehand, the more likely you are to pay once and regret it afterwards. That is exactly how I feel: I would like my money back.

Conclusion: Practically useless for serious task management or ADHD support. Clear verdict: Stay away.

title: Overcome ADHD????
body:
The title is already a massive red flag: “Overcoming ADHD”. You don’t overcome ADHD. You learn to understand your brain and work with it.

I was actually quite excited by the idea of an AI designed specifically for ADHD minds. Something that adapts to the way you think, helps you organise, plan and break things down in a way that works for you. But instead, the whole introduction is incredibly negative and condescending towards ADHD, repeatedly presenting it as something that needs fixing.

I find this particularly insulting when you consider the audience they’re targeting. Many young ADHDers are already struggling with confidence, frustration and understanding themselves. They need encouragement and tools that help them recognise their strengths, not another product telling them their brains need repairing.

And then there’s the business model: you can’t properly try the application before committing to a full year’s subscription. Given the impulsivity and memory difficulties that can come with ADHD, that’s a pretty questionable approach.

I didn’t fall for it, but I’ve seen reviews from people who have paid for a year and can’t even use the app.

An application designed for ADHD should start by understanding ADHD. There’s so much beauty in these brains: creativity, imagination, empathy and different ways of thinking. How about building something that works WITH those differences rather than selling people the idea that they need to overcome them?

When you first get the app, it immediately makes you take an extensive survey where you give them tons of personal info. title: game changer if you’re often in high pressure situations
body: for context: i work in a high stress environment, and am in a senior management position. i’ve been using an executive coach for quite some time now, given it’s difficult to juggle my role with (at times) pretty crippling ADHD. recently downloaded this app to help me when i don’t have access to my coach, and I’ve gotta say… seriously considering replacing my coach with this app. it’s absolutely key to helping me break down my tasks, stay focused, and manage my day/direct reports in a way that actually works for my ADHD brain. author: dodgerblue_

author: Jlinks17

title: A Lifesaver for ADHD!
body:
Mindflow AI is exactly what I needed - a calming, intelligent voice companion that helps me manage the chaos of ADHD. It feels like having a supportive friend who’s always there to guide me through distractions, being overwhelmed, and emotional ups and downs.
The app adapts to how I’m feeling each day and offers personalized reminders, focus support, and even just someone to talk to and I need grounding. It’s not just another productivity app, it gets how ADHD actually works.
Highly recommend if you want real dash time support, structure, without pressure, and a judgment free tool to help you stay on track. Total game changer!
author: J. Bragg-Harris

title: Super Helpful!
body: I rarely leave reviews, but I felt compelled to share my experience with Mindflow. It’s been a surprisingly powerful tool, especially for someone managing ADHD. I wish more therapists and coaches recommended it as a helpful companion between sessions. Within days, I started noticing patterns in my behavior that I’d never been able to pinpoint. The customized insights helped me look at long-standing habits in a new light. I’ve already told a few friends about it—definitely worth checking out.
author: Andrew374

author: dRodriguez6767

title: 10/10 helps with organizing my life
body: I'm not diagnosed with ADHD but but I often get overwhelmed with tons of tasks on my TODO list. Mindflow has completely changed how I handle my day. It’s a great way to structure tasks and mentally organize what's ahead, significantly reducing my mental overhead and anxiety around doing this alone. Sometimes I miss a day here or there but always come back and love how Mindflow remembers everything so we can pick back up immediately. Also love chat mode for when I’m in public places vs live mode for when I want to work through things realtime.
author: Alexander Shaq

title: Love this app!
body: I was diagnosed with ADHD at 24, and Mindflow has helped me understand my brain in ways I never could on my own. Everything is genuinely relatable and feels custom-made for my daily challenges. The app delivers insightful content in a much easier-to-digest format compared to diving into books or lengthy articles about ADHD.
author: jaltaire

title: So good
body: I almost never write app reviews, but Mindflow truly deserves it. Honestly, I don't understand why this isn't recommended more by ADHD coaches or therapists as supplementary guidance between sessions. Instantly, I gained real insights about habits I've struggled with forever. After just a few days of usage, the personalized feedback had me genuinely rethinking some behaviors. Now I started sharing this app with friends. definitely worth giving this a shot.
author: lpj667

body: I've been using Mindflow for 4 days now. So far, the interactive assessments are fantastic, especially those helping me pinpoint specific triggers behind my ADHD symptoms and better understand how my mind works. Also, the AI voice companion is seriously impressive and provided immediate, helpful answers to all my questions. Out of every app I've tried with an AI component, this is hands-down one of the best.
